Existing reviewed input/Send profiles are not structural-mount authorization. A future structural Shadow host must add no new Trusted Types HTML sink. Prefer a DOM-built in-flow host/Shadow subtree, preserve the named-policy boundary, keep MV3 structural mounting viable in the default isolated content-script world, and do not require MAIN-world/unsafeWindow authority. Browser TT support is broad in 2026, but host CSP enforcement remains site-specific and is not inferred for every adapter.

Open Shadow DOM isolates implementation/style but not UA UI-event propagation. Future Blue/Red certification must not assume clicks are contained: passive mount/repair stays zero-actuation, intentional Ghost activation must cause exactly one reviewed Ghost action and zero host Send/submit/native-control side effects, delegatesFocus stays false initially, mount/repair never autofocuses or steals editor focus, every Ghost button is type=button, and cross-portal ARIA IDREF relationships are accepted only when exact DOM/accessibility-tree evidence proves them.

Before judging a real A2 candidate, the harness must prove its own sensitivity by rejecting deliberately unsafe synthetic adapters for wrong-composer selection, Send identity/movement, overlay mounting, duplicate/stale repair, unscoped observers, incomplete cleanup, new TT sinks, focus/form side effects, inaccessible cross-root claims, and viewport-placement authority. verificationSummary.crossAdapterConstraints: Reviewed actuation/input profiles do not grant structural mutation authority. Use three evidence stages: anchor smoke (no mutation authority), adapter-specific authenticated structural capture, then mount certification. A certified site-specific runner may outrank the standard structural protocol only when reviewed site identity plus current structural capability/signature checks pass and predeclared evidence shows measurable benefit. Shared code may own invariant checks/repair/teardown, but each adapter owns structural discovery and approved insertion rules. Specialized verification failure demotes to the standard adapter-aware structural protocol; missing/failed standard structural capability means rail-only. No non-ChatGPT adapter inherits ChatGPT's insertion rule by analogy.
verificationSummary.siteSpecificFirstRunnerPolicy: Runner order: (1) certified site-specific structural runner when site identity and current certified structure checks both pass; (2) standard adapter-aware structural protocol; (3) existing rail fallback. A specialized runner earns first position through measurable superiority such as fewer DOM assumptions, exact Send preservation, smaller observer churn, native reachability/mobile reflow, exact teardown, cross-browser falsification, and maintenance resilience. Hostname alone and reviewed Send authority are insufficient.
verificationSummary.compatibilityConstraints: Future structural shell must add no new Trusted Types HTML sink. The deterministic prototype uses DOM-created Shadow nodes and textContent, not shadowRoot.innerHTML. Preserve the existing named-policy boundary, avoid a permissive default policy, keep extension mounting viable in isolated content-script world, and do not require unsafeWindow/MAIN-world authority. Existing whole-product blocked-policy behavior remains fail-loud and is not reclassified as a current PASS.
verificationSummary.interactionAccessibilityConstraints: Shadow DOM is not an event-safety boundary. verificationSummary.accessibilityVerificationConstraints: Tier A uses one locator-scoped Playwright ARIA semantic contract across hosted Chromium and desktop Firefox plus exact focus traversal, Send-node identity, role/name/state, expanded-state, hidden-content, cleanup, and zero-actuation invariants. Tier C keeps TalkBack, VoiceOver, NVDA/JAWS, WebView, GeckoView, and other physical/platform AT mappings separately uncertified until explicitly tested. Do not use browser-specific expected snapshots as a default escape hatch for deterministic semantic divergence, do not auto-update snapshots unattended to bless a mismatch, and do not treat Playwright ARIA snapshots as sufficient proof of peer-ShadowRoot aria-controls relationships.
